description: Extract functions, data types, and interfaces from legacy codebase to build functional inventory

artifacts.description: Extracted functions with signatures and dependencies

actions.description: Review the languages, frameworks, and entry points identified in RE-01
actions.llm_guidance: Read specs/reverse/codebase_inventory.json and note the primary language, largest files, and detected entry points

actions.description: For each source file, extract function/method definitions
actions.llm_guidance:
For each major source file, identify:
- Function/method names
- Parameters and return types
- Dependencies (calls to other functions)
- Purpose (inferred from name and code)

Language-specific patterns:
- Python: def, class methods
- Java: public/private methods
- C/C++: function definitions
- Fortran: subroutine, function, program
- JavaScript: function, arrow functions, class methods

actions.description: Identify structs, classes, types, and data structures
actions.llm_guidance:
For each source file, identify:
- Class/struct definitions
- Type aliases
- Enums
- Data structures and their fields
- Inheritance relationships

For each function, identify:
- Functions it calls
- Global state it accesses
- External dependencies (libraries)
- I/O operations

Categorize each function as:
- pure: No side effects, deterministic output
- stateful: Modifies internal state
- io: Performs file/network/display operations
- coordination: Orchestrates other functions

actions.description: Compile all extracted information into structured JSON
actions.llm_guidance:
Create specs/reverse/extracted_functions.json with:
- functions array (name, type, inputs, outputs, dependencies, source_location)
- data_types array (name, attributes, relationships)
- dependency_graph (function -> [called_functions])

criteria: At least 80% of source files analyzed
All entry points have functions extracted
Dependency graph is complete (no dangling references)

notes: For large codebases (>10K LOC), prioritize entry points and high-dependency modules first. Use sampling for very large files.
